data.description: The C11-192 classification of Sentry issue C11-31 shows SwiftUI/AttributeGraph graph work as the largest hang family (559 of 875 captures, pre-#401 per-capture counts: 291 hosting-begin-transaction, 179 hosting-layout). C11-191 (tab bar preference-pass stall) is one member of this family, not the whole of it. Once C11-192's classifier ships, main-thread-hang/swiftui-update/* exist as separate Sentry issues with their own user counts. Work: read the per-phase trend after the first post-classifier release, pick the dominant phase, and profile/fix it specifically. Blocked-by relationship in spirit on C11-192's PR #402 landing; do not start until the per-phase trend exists. Acceptance: a profile identifying the concrete c11 view-tree or hosting path responsible for the dominant phase, a fix, and a declining distinct-user trend on that phase's Sentry issue.
data.title: SwiftUI graph-work hangs: split hosting-begin-transaction vs hosting-layout and attack the dominant phase

data.body:
PARKED: data-blocked on the 0.63.0 release (operator decision 2026-08-10).

The per-phase trend this ticket waits on does not exist. The classifier (#402, merged 2026-08-04) rides in 0.63.0, which has never been publicly released: latest published release is v0.61.0 (2026-07-29), and 'git tag --contains 5920e3bb0' returns no version tag. Real users are on 0.58.0 and 0.61.0. Every main-thread-hang/* Sentry issue combined holds 7 events from a single maintainer machine, all staging.rel.v0.63.0 or debug builds. There is no swiftui-update/hosting-layout issue at all.

What IS known now, from the C11-199 offline reclassification of the full 4,763-event C11-30/C11-31 corpus (20 distinct users, 2026-07-25 to 2026-08-10): swiftui-update is confirmed as the dominant family in real user data, 2,653 events from 17 of 20 users, 1,554 episodes, median stall 3,128 ms. The hosting-begin-transaction vs hosting-layout split is NOT recoverable from that corpus, because shipped releases send only stack.prefix(24) on the wire while phaseRules scan the full 96-frame capture. So the phase question specifically does require the classifier in users' hands.

Unblock condition: publish a release carrying #402, then read the per-phase distinct-user counts. Operator has queued a release pass. Resume once that trend exists.

Also relevant to the future baseline: C11-191/#411 already stopped late heartbeats reporting as hangs, and C11-198/#413 narrows runloop-idle.
